frequency_question: How often does structural friction prevent or delay the implementation of announced or contemplated extraordinary liquidity management tools within the target window?
membership_rule: Members are defined as policy actions specifically targeting excess liquidity via quantitative reserve ratio adjustments or special deposit mechanisms by central banks of systemic emerging economies (e.g., RBI, PBOC, Bank Indonesia) during surplus liquidity regimes. Excluded are standard open market operations and regular benchmark interest rate adjustments.
window: A rolling 35-day execution window during liquidity surplus cycles.

cases.name: PBOC reserve requirement ratio hike for liquidity management
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement adjustment
RBI incremental CRR consideration without execution due to sudden banking stress
PBOC targeted RRR deployment delayed by interbank friction

coverage_note: 5 named cases representing major emerging market liquidity tool implementations; estimated total population across emerging markets in past two decades is approximately 12.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unannounced fine-tuning operations and developed market equivalents where institutional transmission mechanisms differ significantly.
skeleton: Total documented extraordinary liquidity absorption policy attempts divided into successful executions within the target execution window versus those delayed or abandoned due to structural plumbing friction.
multiplier: 3 hits / 5 total attempts = 60% base implementation success rate under structural friction constraints.
validity_reason: Central bank operational frameworks and interbank market plumbing structures evolve slowly over multi-year horizons.
